item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.8
item.description:
Review shows what changed

The review card is bigger and shows, top to bottom:

  • As sent — the note's lines as the agent received them, with a few lines of context either side.
  • Now — the same lines as they are today. When nothing changed it says so in one line; when the text was removed the sent lines are struck.
  • The agent's reply.
  • A follow-up field that is always there. Return adds the follow-up; what you type is kept per note while you step through.
  • The buttons: previous and next, Accept All…, Later, Follow Up and Accept.

Pictures, PDFs and whole-file notes show no excerpts; the document behind the card is what to look at.

To make "As sent" possible, every delivered send now remembers the note's lines at that moment. Notes sent before this release show only "Now" until they are sent again.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.7
item.description:
A fix for the sixth beta.

Fixed

  • A long Markdown page with a table in it scrolls to its end again. Since 0.6.0-beta.6 it stopped after the first screen.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.6
item.description:
The sixth beta: one font size for everything, tables that scroll, and a quick way to note a whole file.

New

  • Notes on the whole file. A composer at the bottom of the notes panel takes a note about the file in front of you, not a passage in it. It's a draft like any other, sent and reviewed the same way, and the agent reads the file itself. Notes › New Note on Whole File opens it too.
  • Wide tables scroll sideways. Tables line up with the text on the left. One too wide for the page scrolls within it, with a scroller that shows while you scroll and soft fades at the edges. Selecting, Find and notes work in the hidden cells as well.

Changed

  • One font size. Settings › Editor has a single Font size (9–24 pt, 13 by default) that sets code, plain text, Markdown source and rendered pages, and spreadsheets. Headings, code blocks, line numbers and spreadsheet headers scale with it. Web pages, PDFs and themes that set their own size keep it. A code size you changed before carries over.
  • Page width in one place. Page width and Fill the window sit with the font size in Settings › Editor, and text fills the page. Jira issues, Confluence pages and pull request descriptions follow them too.

Fixed

  • Gloss no longer crashes when you switch from a Markdown file to another file after adding a note.
  • Line numbers widen with the font size, and jumping to a line centers it.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.5
item.description:
The fifth beta: rendered Markdown that is easier to read, and tables that finally fit.

New

  • Tables with real columns. Columns keep their natural width when they fit; otherwise long cells wrap inside their column, and a word too long for any column (a URL, say) breaks rather than pushing the table off the page. Tables have column lines, a shaded header, striped rows and rounded corners, and HTML tables look the same. Notes, Find and highlights work in table cells, and copying table rows gives you tab-separated cells in order.
  • Rendered Markdown settings. Settings › Editor › Rendered Markdown sets the text size (12–20 pt), how wide tables may grow (600–1600 pt), or lets them fill the window.

Changed

  • A comfortable line length. Text stops at about 90 characters, centered, however wide the window is, and grows with the text size. Tables wider than the text spread out on both sides of it.
  • More room to read. Lines are a little taller, headings and paragraphs have more space around them, and the spacing grows with the text size.
  • The page lays itself out again once a window resize ends, without flickering while you drag.

Fixed

  • The pointer over the Review card is an arrow again, not a text cursor.
  • Accept and Accept All no longer stay disabled while a slow follow-up send is still going through. Accept All is now drawn as a button, not as gray text that looked disabled.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.4
item.description:
The fourth beta: choose whether the notes panel lists the file in front or the whole location.

New

  • This File | This Location. A bar at the bottom of the notes panel switches the list between the notes on the file you're looking at and the notes on every file in the location. Gloss remembers your choice; This Location is the default. It changes only the list: Send keeps its own This File / This Location in its menu.
  • A note count. The same bar shows how many notes the list is showing, with your filters and search applied.

Changed

  • The bar under the viewer keeps one height, so it no longer shifts when the follow and path buttons appear.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.3
item.description:
The third beta: Gloss is open source under the MIT License.

New

  • Open source. The code is on GitHub under the MIT License. Help › Acknowledgments lists the licenses of the packages Gloss is built on.
  • Updates without a GitHub key. Gloss now checks for and downloads updates from the public repository, so Check for Updates works with no GitHub key in Settings › Integrations. Your key is now only for pull requests and for sending feedback from the app.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.2
item.description:
The second beta: theme your syntax highlighting, and paths for text notes on web pages.

New

  • Syntax themes. In Settings › Themes, pick one theme for light mode and one for dark. Gloss, the default, looks just as before; eight more come built in (Solar, Balanced, Earth, Frost and Midnight). A theme sets the colors of each kind of code (with bold and italic), the editor's background, selection, current line and line numbers, and the code font. Duplicate a theme to edit it, with live previews and a warning when something is hard to read. Import themes from Xcode, TextMate or VS Code, and export your own. Themes apply to the editor, Markdown source, code blocks in rendered Markdown, the minimap, and code excerpts in notes.

Fixed

  • Text notes on a rendered web page now get an outline and a path to their card, like element notes, as you scroll and resize.

Sharing still hasn't been tried between two Macs.

item.title: Gloss 0.6.0-beta.1
item.description:
A beta: the agent can refine a document with you in rounds, and you can share a document and its notes with someone else through iCloud Drive.

New

  • Refinement. Notes › Refine This Document asks the agent to read the document and ask you about anything unclear, as anchored questions. Answer them, by choosing from the agent's options or in your own words, and press Send at the end of each round. The agent keeps asking until it has no more questions and has made its changes, then says it's done. End it at any time; its questions stay as ordinary notes.
  • Questions with choices. An agent's question can offer one or several options to pick from, alongside a written answer.
  • Share a review. Share in the toolbar (or File › Share…) puts the document and its sent notes in a .gloss file in iCloud Drive. Collaborate shares that file, so both of you work on the same review; Send a Copy sends a separate one. Shared reviews open under Reviews.
  • Who wrote what. In a shared review every note and reply shows its author. Set your name in Settings. A collaborator's Send goes to the owner, and only the owner sends to an agent.

Changed

  • A new iteration starts when the last note is resolved only if the content actually changed, so a round of questions no longer starts one. It's a setting in Settings › Notes, on by default.

Fixed

  • The Review card now draws above note outlines and paths.

This is a beta: sharing hasn't yet been tried between two Macs.

item.title: Gloss 0.5.0
item.description:
Review what your agent did, see every iteration's notes, preview a packet before sending it, and a compact layout for narrow windows.

New

  • Review When Done. Turn it on in the Send menu and the agent says what it changed for each note. Each note it resolves stays highlighted until you've looked at it; Review steps through them, and you accept each one or follow up.
  • All Iterations. In the iteration menu, list every iteration's notes in the notes panel, newest first, under a header for each iteration.
  • Show Earlier Notes. Earlier iterations' notes are drawn in the document with dashed outlines, found again in the file as it is now. Click one in the gutter to read it.
  • Preview Packet. In the Send menu, or Notes › Preview Packet… (⌥⌘↩): see exactly what Send will hand over, readable or raw, and which drafts the scope leaves out and why. Copy it or send it from there.
  • Each folder remembers where you were. Switching folders brings back that folder's last file, where you were reading, its selected notes, and the panel's tab, colors and search. A folder you haven't visited starts empty.
  • Compact layout. In a narrow window, the explorer slides over the document and the notes panel becomes a tray under it: one line with the current note, steps through the notes, and Send. Open the tray for the whole panel. Choose Automatic, Always Compact or Always Full, and the width, in Settings › General › Layout or View › Layout.
  • App icon follows light and dark mode. In Settings › General, pick one icon for light mode and another for dark.

Changed

  • The menus are reorganized: About and Check for Updates are in the Gloss menu, searches in Edit, display options and Layout in View, navigation in Go, and note and iteration actions in Notes.

item.title: Gloss 0.4.1
item.description:
A tidier location dropdown, and Follow moves under the file tree.

Changed

  • In the location dropdown, a folder's controls show only when you point at it: a star adds it to Favorites, a slashed star under Favorites removes it, and the close button closes an open folder. They line up from row to row.
  • Favorites no longer show a star of their own.
  • The Follow crosshair now sits in the bar under the file tree, beside the hidden-files toggle.

item.title: Gloss 0.4.0
item.description:
Rounds of review, a safety net for deleted notes, and a notes panel that follows the folder you're in.

New

  • Iterations. Each file's notes come in numbered rounds. Start a new iteration from the menu in the file's header, choose whether open notes come along, and look back at any earlier round: the file as it was, its notes where they were taken, and the lines changed since. Gloss keeps its own snapshots and never writes to your repository. Settings › Notes can start a new round after every note is resolved, or when a file's git commit changes.
  • Recently Deleted. Deleted notes go to Recently Deleted in the notes panel's menu, where you can restore them with their threads or delete them for good. They're kept for 30 days by default.
  • Mermaid diagrams draw in the rendered Markdown view, in light and dark, and you can add notes to a region of a diagram.
  • Renames keep your notes. Renaming a file or folder in Gloss carries its notes, iterations and unsaved edits to the new name.

Changed

  • The notes panel shows the notes of the folder in front; switching folders hides the others without touching them.
  • Send has a menu built in: pick This File or This Location, or copy the same notes as a packet.
  • Selecting adjacent notes draws one outline around them, blending their colors.
  • The location dropdown lists your favorites from every host, and opening one on another host connects first.
  • When the chosen agent isn't running any more, the picker marks it instead of quietly picking another.
  • New File and New Folder never replace something that's already there.

Fixed

  • A send that's called off because the folder or notes changed says why, instead of showing as a failed delivery.
  • Edits to a file opened under /tmp reload as they happen.

item.title: Gloss 0.3.0
item.description:
Notes become conversations: you and your agent can go back and forth on a note until it's done.

New

  • Each note is a thread. Write a follow-up on a sent note and send it; the agent gets what it said and what you replied. A follow-up reopens a resolved note.
  • Agents can reply and ask. With reply_to_note an agent answers without closing the note, or asks you something back, and the card shows Your turn.
  • Notes follow the agent's edits. When an agent rewrites the text a note is on, it says where the change went and the highlight moves there. The card says Edited by the agent, and Restore Original puts it back. Where the text was removed, the note becomes a caret at that spot.
  • Separate Resolved Notes in the notes panel's menu lists open notes above resolved ones, with a thin rule between them.

Changed

  • A selected card is outlined in its note's colour instead of a blue band.
  • A collapsed card shows the whole of the latest message; the chevron points up while a card is open.
  • Each turn is headed only with who wrote it: the agent's name or You.
  • Agents resolve a note without a message when the change speaks for itself.
  • The selection bar appears only when two or more notes are selected.

Fixed

  • Paths to cards draw as soon as a window opens, without selecting a note first.
  • Clicking a card's follow-up field keeps the keyboard there.

item.title: Gloss 0.2.0
item.description:
A big round: web pages are first-class, notes are calmer to work through, and rendered Markdown looks like it does on GitHub.

New

  • Web pages in the window. Click the title to type an address or a path; Open Quickly takes URLs too, and the explorer's Web host lists the pages you've visited.
  • Notes on pictures and elements of a web page. Click a picture to note all of it, or drag across it to note a region, as in Markdown and image files. Pick Element (Notes › Pick Element on Page, ⇧⌘E) notes any element; ↑ and ↓ step to its parent or child. The agent gets the picture's size, the region and a crop.
  • Notes on pictures in Markdown, a region or the whole picture.
  • Markdown renders as GitHub does: the HTML READMEs use, pictures from the web, and GIFs that play.
  • Hosts and Follow live in the folder dropdown above the file tree. It lists This Mac, Web, GitHub, Atlassian and your ssh hosts with their connection state, and Follow sits beside it, lit while on (also Go › Follow Herdr).
  • Act on several notes at once from the notes panel, put a sent note back to a draft, and edit a note in its card.
  • Show or hide resolved notes, and the page draws only the notes the panel lists.
  • The folder's agent is picked for you at launch and whenever the folder changes.
  • Jira issues show their titles in the explorer.
  • What was open comes back at launch.
  • A new app icon, with 16 styles to choose from in Settings.

Changed

  • Each note in the packet starts with its id (Note: n_…), so agents can resolve it without searching.
  • Gloss says when an agent's set-up needs updating and opens Settings › Agents on it; press Update there.
  • An agent's reply is headed with the agent that resolved it, and a card shows the latest turn of its thread with the rest a click away.
  • Sent notes step back and drafts stand out; paths meet the middle of a card's colour bar.
  • The notes panel's Send is back for this document's drafts.

Fixed

  • An agent can resolve a note whose text it removed.
  • Note outlines no longer sit in the wrong place when a rendered Markdown file first opens.
  • Escape puts away the Add Note button and cancels the composer.

item.title: Gloss 0.1.2
item.description:
Fixes for the first round of reports from 0.1.1, plus a few new things.

Fixed

  • Drafts only leave Gloss when you press Send. The Claude Code and Codex prompt hook could hand every draft in a folder to the agent, unseen, whenever a prompt was submitted (including the prompt a send itself submits) and mark them sent. The hook is gone. After updating, open Settings › Agents and press Update on Claude Code and Codex to remove it from their settings (a backup is kept). Agents now only see notes you've sent them, and Copy as Packet leaves notes as drafts.
  • Notes keep their place when files change. When a note's text appears in several places, Gloss picks the one whose surrounding lines match, and flags the note for a look when it can't be sure. A file changed while it was closed has its notes found again when it opens. A sent note that loses its text and finds it again stays sent; a resolved note stays resolved.
  • The notes filter bar no longer wraps when the panel is narrow: it drops the title, then the counts.

New

  • Back and Forward through the documents you've viewed, across folders and hosts: Go › Back (⌃⌘←) and Forward (⌃⌘→), or the chevrons in the toolbar.
  • Agents can show you things. Over MCP an agent can ask you a question beside the lines it's about (it waits under Attention; reply and send to answer), open a file at a range of lines, and add a project folder to your favorites.
  • Images in Jira issues and Confluence pages show inline, and attached images and PDFs open in their viewers so you can note a region of them.
  • Paths from notes to cards are smoother and move exactly with the page.

item.title: Gloss 0.1.1
item.description:
First release of Gloss.

  • Browse folders on this Mac and over ssh, and annotate any region of any file
  • Send notes to Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
  • Review pull requests, Jira issues and Confluence pages
  • Updates and in-app feedback
